spec.note: A — LLM trần, không tool, không triage (sàn dưới)

findings.issue: Path traversal via user-controlled cookie value allows reading arbitrary files on the server (CWE-22).
Path traversal via client-controlled cookie value leading to arbitrary file write/overwrite
Trust boundary violation: client-controlled cookie value is used directly as a session attribute name without validation

findings.snippet:
userCookie.setPath(request.getRequestURI());
        userCookie.setDomain(new java.net.URL(request.getRequestURL().toString()).getHost());
findings.issue: Cookie Domain/Path attributes derived from attacker-controlled Host header and request URI
Use of weak/broken DES cryptographic algorithm to protect sensitive data
Stack trace and internal exception details exposed to the client
OS command injection via attacker-controlled HTTP header concatenated into a shell command
OS command injection / untrusted environment variable injection into Runtime.exec
SQL injection via attacker-controlled HTTP header concatenated into a CallableStatement query

findings.snippet:
int randNumber = java.security.SecureRandom.getInstance("SHA1PRNG").nextInt(99);
            String rememberMeKey = Integer.toString(randNumber);
findings.issue: Weak randomness in remember-me authentication token allows trivial brute-force forgery of the remember-me cookie
Path traversal via unvalidated, attacker-controlled HTTP header used to construct a java.io.File path (information disclosure through existence checks)
LDAP injection via unescaped request header value concatenated into LDAP search filter

findings.snippet: String filter = "(&(objectclass=person))(|(uid=" + param + ")(street={0}))";
findings.issue: Unescaped LDAP filter string constructed with attacker-controlled parameter
Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via unescaped Referer header written to an HTML response
Externally controlled format string can trigger unhandled exceptions (denial of service)
Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): attacker-controlled Referer header is written directly into an HTML response without encoding
OS command injection via attacker-controlled HTTP header concatenated into a shell command
HTTP response splitting / cookie injection via URL-decoded, unvalidated request header placed directly into a Set-Cookie value
OS command injection via attacker-controlled HTTP header concatenated into Runtime.exec()
SQL injection via unsanitized HTTP header value concatenated into SQL INSERT statement
